title: Quadratic Inequalities
short: Use the zeros and the graph to find where a quadratic is positive or negative.
trouble: Students solve x² > 4 as x > ±2 instead of x < −2 or x > 2.

blocks.html: To solve $x^2 - x - 6 > 0$ you need every $x$ that makes the expression positive. The zeros are the only places the sign can change, so they split the number line into pieces. This connects to Compound Inequalities: the answer is often an "or."

Move everything to one side, find the zeros, and mark them on a number line. The sign is the same throughout each piece, so test one number per piece (or picture the parabola). Keep the pieces with the sign you want; include the zeros only for $\ge$ or $\le$.

A polynomial graph is an unbroken curve, so it can't jump from positive to negative without passing through 0. Between two neighboring zeros the curve stays on one side of the $x$-axis. For a parabola that opens up, it is below the axis between its zeros and above outside them.

blocks.name: alg2-signchart
blocks.cap: $(x + 2)(x - 3) > 0$. Each factor changes sign at its zero; the product is positive where the signs agree. Drag the gold test line.

blocks.name: parabola
blocks.cap: The same inequality as a graph: $y = x^2 - x - 6$ is above the $x$-axis to the left of $-2$ and to the right of $3$.

blocks.title: Outside the zeros
steps: Test $x = 0$: $(2)(-3) = -6$, negative. Test $x = 4$: $(6)(1) = 6$, positive. Test $x = -3$: $(-1)(-6) = 6$, positive.
Keep the positive pieces. The zeros make it 0, which is not $> 0$.

blocks.title: The trap with squares
steps: Between the zeros the product is negative; at the zeros it is 0. Both are allowed.

blocks.title: A parabola that opens down
steps: This parabola opens down, so it is above the axis between its zeros.

blocks.html: Solving $x^2 > 4$ as $x > \pm 2$. That would say $x > -2$, which includes $x = 0$, and $0^2 > 4$ is false. The two zeros point in opposite directions: $x < -2$ or $x > 2$. Always test a number from each piece in the original inequality.
